annotations.text:
How far a running card has come — the comp to sign before the build.
The intent, in the owner's words: the progress of the task list as the live session reports it, on the collapsed card. The task list is the plan's items; the session marks each one in its own copy of the plan when its "done means" holds; the board reads that copy and shows the count. Once every item is met, the same line counts the review loop — pass, found, fixed, filed — from the review record the lane writes pass by pass.
Staged: the four items on the storm-warning plan (Harbourmaster's fixture plans carry one promise each), the deviated stance, the review passes, the times and slots. Assumed: the signed colour language and card anatomy — only the strip row, the counter line and the two open-card sections are new.

The head's "Executing · 1 of 3" on the first open card is the card's position in its column, exactly as signed. Beside a count of items it can misread; the review card drops it to show the difference. Say which reads right.
